rubric.result: Seven sentences in ### Desired end state, and the sum of the thirteen commits produces every one of them. (1) GET /spec-freeze answers four states, all derived and none stored: SpecFreezeRoute.reading returns {status:'none'} with no held session, and ReadSpecFreeze.execute computes no-spec / draft / frozen on the call from EpicSpecs.mostRecent, EpicSpec.isFrozen() and, only on the frozen branch, EpicBranch.current + PullRequests.openOfBranch (D-13 honoured: nothing is written down). (2) The findings are analyzeSpecFreeze's own: EpicSpec.findings() imports analyzeSpecFreeze and HYPOTHESIS_REASONS from plugin/scripts/groom.js and projects them exhaustively into FreezeFinding, one per clarification with its line and raw text, one for ABSENT and one for EMPTY; the route wires them out with code/line/detail untouched, and the diff adds no second opinion (the global control 'no analyzeSpecFreeze under backend/src/infrastructure' is green). (3) POST /spec-freeze writes the two header lines (EpicSpec.frozenAt), commits both documents, pushes the checkout's branch and opens the pull request naming both paths in its body, and answers the date and that pull request. (4) The five refusals exist with their {code, detail}: gate-not-from-the-page (403, before the freeze is asked), no-coordinating-session, no-epic-spec, spec-already-frozen and spec-not-freezable, and all five return before specs.rewrite. (5) GitEpicBranch.publish resolves the branch and the remote's default and throws EpicBranchNotPublished before any add, commit or push. (6) Home renders <SpecFreezePanel /> after the home__sessions section and outside every currentStage branch; the panel lists the findings, disables the button while findings remain or no key was handed, and on frozen renders the date, the pull request anchor and 'El groom espera al merge de este pull request.'. (7) PhasePrompt.FREEZE_IS_NOT_YOURS sits between the checkout line and the idea in every brainstorming prompt. Measured with the four defects the run already recorded in .agent/SLICE.md (A, B, C, D) held out of this item as the launching agent directed and as they were raised inside the run: A and C are the two that bear on this sentence-by-sentence reading — with C standing, the real page reads key:null and the button never enables — and both are scheduled as ordinary commits on this branch. I found no eighth promise that the sum of the diff leaves absent.

Thirteen task commits plus two merges of origin/main (620b791 and 2571020, which bring #342, #344 and #345 into the accumulated diff without any task's hand in them). Read in order, each commit leaves standing what the ones before it established and no reversal is unaccounted for. The two places where a later commit rewrote an earlier decision are both single-decision consolidations the objectives asked for: task 3 moved the default-branch parse out of GitWorkspace#declaredBase into the public GitWorkspace.declaredBranchIn and made #declaredBase call it, and task 4 turned GhPullRequests#openOf into a delegation to the new openOfBranch so one place runs 'pr list' (both greps in section 8 are green). The freeze yardstick is asked once and in one place: EpicSpec.isFreezable() wraps the same findings() the query reads, so tasks 5 and 6 do not decide freezability twice. The wiring of task 9 mounts exactly the handlers tasks 7 and 8 exported, and ct-api builds one DiskEpicSpecs, one GitEpicBranch and one GateKey shared by the query and the action. The merge of origin/main did not undo task work: Home.tsx carries both <SpecFreezePanel /> and #342's presentational CoordinatingSessionStatus/isCoordinatingSessionLive, and SpecFreezePanel keeps its own hook so it does not collide with the lifting. One statement written for an intermediate state did survive its retirement — backend/API.md still says 'no frontend client reads or presses gate 1 yet - this backend-only slice of the epic ... leaves the cabin's panel to a following task', which tasks 11 to 13 falsified, and the two rows the plan asked for in 'Where the frontend consumes each one' are still absent. I do not charge it here: the judge of task 10 already recorded it as a low finding, naming this exact consequence, and one defect is one finding.

The declared signal is 'the spec commit carries `Estado: CONGELADA` with its date and a refusal names the offending line', and both halves are produced by production lines of this diff. Emission: EpicSpec.frozenAt(on) rewrites the two header lines, DiskEpicSpecs.rewrite puts that text on disk and GitEpicBranch #add/#commit put it in the commit git-epic-branch.ts composes, so the commit gate 1 makes carries the state line and the date; SpecFreezeRefusal.#notFreezableDetail composes 'the spec is not freezable: <n> finding(s) remain, the first on line <line>' (and '..., the first is <code>' when the finding has none), which Answer.refuseAs sends as the spec-not-freezable body and SpecFreezePanel renders untranslated in its error Banner. Neither half lives only in a test. Instrumentation: this signal is not a metric or a log line, and the repository ships no emit library for one; both halves are produced through the repository's own existing means - the Gh/git ToolLaunch adapters and the Answer/Refusal {code, detail} doctrine of backend/conventions/this-repository.md - so the slice brings nothing of its own to emit with. Cardinality: the signal carries no label or dimension; the only variable values are a calendar date (EpicSpec.dateOf, the local day) and a line number, both bounded. No smell: the diff does test both halves (freeze-spec.test.ts asserts the text handed to rewrite, spec-freeze-route.test.ts asserts 'a refused freeze names the offending line in its detail'), but what the cell names does not end with that run - the state line is read in production after the merge, by EpicSpec.isFrozen() on every two-second poll of GET /spec-freeze and by the panel that prints the date, and the refusal detail is read by the person who pressed the button - so the second half of the smell does not hold and the cell is a signal doing its job, not a restated acceptance criterion.
